**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Persist progress while skipping shadow candidates**

When the candidate set takes longer than the 90-second deadline to scan and a previously attempted evidence row before the cursor acquires a new input context, skipped rows never advance any durable cursor because `cursor_run` is derived only from newly inserted `EvidenceJudgeRun` records. Each invocation can therefore wrap to the same prefix, time out before reaching the changed row, and repeat indefinitely. Fresh evidence in the repaired implementation is that pagination was added, but traversal progress is still not persisted when an existing `input_key` is skipped; maintain a separate scan cursor or otherwise checkpoint skipped pages.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply the ordered project-lock protocol to structured matching**

During a retained-news reassignment involving an old project and a different candidate, this loop locks project rows one at a time in UUID order. Concurrent structured ingestion still executes the unordered `select(Project).with_for_update()` in `process_job`; if that scan locks the later UUID first and then waits for the earlier row, this transaction waits for the later row and PostgreSQL detects a deadlock, aborting one ingestion run. Make every multi-project path discover IDs first and acquire project/advisory locks in the same order.
